questions.text: CSS 2017 · Pair: Wrath / Wroth — Which meaning fits “Wrath”?

options.B: (Adjective) relying on someone or something for support; determined by
options.C: Pleasantly warm and mild (of weather or air)

questions.explanation:
Wrath: Extreme anger (noun). Sentence: "The boy feared his father's wrath after he crashed the new car."
Wroth: Angry (archaic/literary adjective, used after a verb). Sentence: "The king was wroth when he learned that his own guards had betrayed him."
Source: CSS 2017 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2017 · Pair: Veracity / Voracity — Which meaning fits “Veracity”?

options.A: Angry (archaic/literary adjective, used after a verb)
options.B: Great eagerness or greed, especially for food
options.D: A thickened, hardened area of skin caused by repeated friction

questions.explanation:
Veracity: Truthfulness; accuracy. Sentence: "The judge doubted the veracity of the witness, whose story changed every time he told it."
Voracity: Great hunger or eagerness; greediness. Sentence: "The voracity of the hungry boys was clear when they finished three plates of biryani in minutes."
Source: CSS 2017 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2017 · Pair: Subtler / Sutler — Which meaning fits “Subtler”?

options.B: Brought into life (past participle of 'bear' used for birth)
options.C: A merchant who sold provisions to soldiers
options.D: A person believed to be able to see the future; a prophet

questions.explanation:
Subtler: More delicate, less obvious (comparative of 'subtle'). Sentence: "The second painting used subtler colours, so its beauty was noticed only on close inspection."
Sutler: A person who followed an army and sold food and supplies to soldiers. Sentence: "In old wars, a sutler travelled behind the troops, selling bread and tobacco at camp."
Source: CSS 2017 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2017 · Pair: Retenue / Retinue — Which meaning fits “Retenue”?

options.A: To cook food slowly in a little liquid in a covered pot
options.B: A short, witty saying expressing a clever idea
options.C: A body of attendants accompanying an important person
options.D: Self-restraint; reserve and discretion in manner (from French)

questions.explanation:
Retenue: Self-restraint; reserve and discretion in manner (from French). Sentence: "Despite the insult, the diplomat showed great retenue and replied in a calm, measured tone."
Retinue: A group of attendants or followers accompanying an important person. Sentence: "The Prime Minister arrived with a retinue of guards, secretaries and advisers."
Source: CSS 2017 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2017 · Pair: Minute / Minuet — Which meaning fits “Minute”?

options.A: To escape or avoid someone or something cleverly; to be hard to grasp
options.B: An underground room or vault beneath a church, used for burial

questions.explanation:
Minute: Extremely small (adjective); also sixty seconds (noun). Sentence: "Only a microscope could reveal the minute cracks in the glass."
Minuet: A slow, graceful dance in triple time, popular in 17th–18th-century Europe; music for it. Sentence: "At the royal ball the couples bowed and stepped gracefully through a minuet."
Source: CSS 2017 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

questions.text: CSS 2017 · Pair: Furor / Furore — Which meaning fits “Furor”?

options.A: A large crowd of people, often disorderly or threatening
options.B: Angry (archaic/literary adjective, used after a verb)
options.D: An outburst of public anger or excitement; also frenzied rage (chiefly American spelling)

questions.explanation:
Furor: An outburst of public anger or excitement; also frenzied rage (chiefly American spelling). Sentence: "The new tax caused a furor among traders, who shut their shops in protest."
Furore: A public uproar or controversy; a sudden craze (British spelling). Sentence: "The referee's decision created a furore in the press, and fans demanded an inquiry."
Source: CSS 2017 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).

options.A: A watery discharge from the eyes or nose

questions.explanation:

questions.text: CSS 2017 · Pair: Bony / Bonny — Which meaning fits “Bony”?

options.A: Very thin so that the bones show; full of bones

questions.explanation:
Bony: Very thin so that the bones show; full of bones. Sentence: "The bony stray dog had clearly not eaten for days."
Bonny: Attractive, healthy-looking (chiefly Scottish/Northern English). Sentence: "The grandmother smiled at the bonny baby with rosy cheeks."
Source: CSS 2017 English Precis & Composition (cssaspirants.pk).
